# StatusPan

> Complete reference for the local daemon and the optional self-hosted relay. StatusPan is one Go binary on loopback, plus an airport-style board. Agents push job updates. StatusPan never pushes back: no nudges, no webhooks, and no board buttons that edit a job. Jobs are removed by Clear all, which asks first, or by a clear control on one section.

Source: <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan>. MIT license. Short version: <https://statuspan.com/llms.txt>. Machine-readable: <https://statuspan.com/openapi.json> and <https://statuspan.com/schema/job-update.schema.json>.

Examples use `MyBot`, `Writer`, `Builder`, `build-1`, `docs-refresh`, `http://127.0.0.1:4477`, `https://example.com`, and `https://relay.example.com`. A real self-hosted relay looks like `https://statuspan-relay.<your-account>.workers.dev`.

## Install and serve

On macOS, [StatusPan.dmg](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg) is a WKWebView window on the local board. It starts the bundled `statuspan serve` if nothing answers on `STATUSPAN_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:4477`), and it stops only a daemon it started. An already-running board is left alone.

The CLI works on macOS and Linux. A short, complete install-and-run sequence also begins <https://statuspan.com/llms.txt> and <https://statuspan.com/skill.md>.

Do these steps in order. This is enough to install StatusPan, start the board, and post a first job.

1. Install the CLI (macOS or Linux):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://statuspan.com/install.sh | sh
```

The installer puts the binary in `/usr/local/bin` when you are root or that directory is writable, otherwise in `~/.local/bin`. It does not edit your shell rc files.

2. Make sure `statuspan` is on PATH:

```bash
command -v statuspan
```

If that prints nothing, add the install directory to PATH, or call the binary by the full path the installer printed:

```bash
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
command -v statuspan
# or run it by full path, for example:
#   ~/.local/bin/statuspan serve
#   /usr/local/bin/statuspan serve
```

To keep PATH for new shells, append that `export` line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. Do not skip this check. `statuspan: command not found` means the install directory is not on PATH.

3. Start the board in the background. It listens only on loopback. The default address is `127.0.0.1:4477`. To use another loopback port (for example if 4477 is already taken), set `STATUSPAN_ADDR`. You can also set `STATUSPAN_DATA` to a separate data directory (default `~/.config/statuspan`):

```bash
export STATUSPAN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:4477
# throwaway port example: export STATUSPAN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:14477
statuspan serve &
```

`statuspan serve --addr 127.0.0.1:14477` is the same as setting `STATUSPAN_ADDR`. Leave the process running.

4. Health-check the board. If the connection is refused, wait a second and try again until you get JSON with a `jobs` array (empty is fine):

```bash
curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"
```

Then open the board at `http://127.0.0.1:4477`, or at whatever host:port you set in `STATUSPAN_ADDR`.

5. Post a test job. If you set `STATUSPAN_ADDR`, `statuspan post` uses it automatically. You can also pass `--addr 127.0.0.1:14477`.

```bash
statuspan post --agent "My Agent" --job hello --state running --note "first post"
```

6. Confirm it shows on the board. Reload the page, or:

```bash
curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"
statuspan ls
```

You should see My Agent / hello as running.

7. Install the agent skill so later sessions can post without this guide:

```bash
statuspan agent install
```

8. Optional: if this machine is not the one running the board, connect it to your relay instead of posting to localhost. See [Connect another machine to your relay](#connect-another-machine-to-your-relay) below, or <https://statuspan.com/relay>.

The installer detects macOS or Linux, arm64 or amd64, and downloads the release binary. It does not edit shell rc files. Then open the board at the address you chose (default <http://127.0.0.1:4477>).

Release files: <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest>.

Raw binaries the installer fetches:

- <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/statuspan-darwin-arm64>
- <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/statuspan-darwin-amd64>
- <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/statuspan-linux-amd64>
- <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/statuspan-linux-arm64>

The disk image is <https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg>.

The board groups Needs attention (failed, blocked, stalled, and abandoned), then In progress. Queued and Done stay folded until opened. Each visible section header can clear that section. Clear all stays in the top menu. `T` toggles day and night.

## What belongs on the board

StatusPan tracks dispatched jobs that have a finish line.

Healthy recurring jobs and scheduled routines stay off the board. Do not clutter it with daily or hourly runs that are going fine.

Exception: if a recurring job becomes `blocked` (it needs human input or approval) or `failed`, push it so it surfaces in Needs attention. A blocked or failed recurring job must be pushed. Once it is fixed or unblocked, push `done` so it clears out of Needs attention.

A routine may still post a separate job when that run produces real, finishable work (for example an inbox check that found a reply to handle). A quiet routine run never appears.

## States

You may post `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `done`, or `failed`.

`stalled` and `abandoned` are not states. They are derived when a job is read. They are not written into the log. Posting either word is a 400: `state must be queued, running, blocked, done, or failed`.

- `queued`: accepted, not started. Does not stall. Abandoned after the waiting window (default 7 days).
- `running`: work in progress. Stalls after `ttl` with no applied heartbeat. Then abandoned after the longer running window.
- `blocked`: a person has to act (approval or input). Shows under Needs attention immediately. Does not stall. Abandoned after the waiting window.
- `done`: finished well. Never abandoned. Folded under Done, so it leaves Needs attention.
- `failed`: finished badly. Never abandoned. Stays under Needs attention until a later applied post moves it (usually `done` once fixed).

A new job must include `state`. A later post may omit it, and the stored state stays.

## Stalled and abandoned

Default `ttl` is 600 seconds (10 minutes), used when a new job omits `ttl`.

Stalled:

- Only `running` can stall. Queued, blocked, done, and failed never stall.
- Stalled when the age since `updated_at` is greater than `ttl` seconds. At the exact threshold it is not stalled yet.
- `ttl` of 0 stalls a running job as soon as the age is greater than zero.
- An abandoned job is not stalled.

Abandoned, also derived, and only after the silence is strictly longer than the threshold. `abandoned_at` is `updated_at` plus that threshold.

- A running job is abandoned only after it is already stalled, once the silence is longer than `max(abandon-after, 4 * ttl)`. Default `abandon-after` is 24h. With `ttl` 7200 (2h), `4 * ttl` is 8h, so the job stalls at 2h and is abandoned at 24h. With a large `ttl`, `4 * ttl` wins when it is longer than 24h. `ttl` 0 uses `abandon-after` alone.
- A queued or blocked job does not stall. It is abandoned after `abandon-waiting-after` (default 168h, 7 days). That window is not multiplied by `ttl`.
- Done and failed are never abandoned.
- At the exact threshold the job is not abandoned yet. One instant later it is.
- Set either window to `0` to disable that category. Set both to `0` to disable auto-abandon. The relay does not take these flags. It always uses 24h and 7 days.
- A new applied post revives the job. `updated_at` moves, and abandoned is computed again, so the job returns to its posted state. An equal or older `seq` stays in history and does not revive it.

`GET /api/jobs` and the daemon SSE snapshot include `abandon_after_seconds` and `abandon_waiting_after_seconds`. `0` means that category is off. The relay job list does not include those two fields. Each job still has `stalled`, `abandoned`, and, when abandoned, `abandoned_at`.

## Payload

`POST` one JSON object, or an array of them. `Content-Type: application/json`. Body limit is 1 MiB (`1048576` bytes). Empty, whitespace, and JSON `null` are `400` `empty body`. A larger body is `400` `body too large`. Broken JSON or a wrong field type is `400` `invalid json`. The relay also rejects a batch of more than 1000 items with `too many updates`. The daemon has no item cap other than the body size.

The batch is validated before anything is written. A validation error writes nothing.

| Field | JSON | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | string | Required. Trimmed blank is `agent is required`. Must not contain `/`, `\`, or NUL (`agent must not contain / or \`). |
| `job_id` | string | Same rules, message says `job_id`. The key is `(agent, job_id)`. |
| `state` | string | Optional on an existing job. One of `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `done`, `failed`. Empty or omitted leaves the stored state. |
| `title` | string | Optional. Omit to leave it. `""` clears it. |
| `progress` | integer | Optional, 0 through 100. Omit to leave it. Out of range: `progress must be an integer from 0 to 100`. |
| `link` | string | Optional. Any string. Not checked as a URL. Omit to leave it. `""` clears it. |
| `note` | string | Optional. Omit to leave it. `""` clears it. |
| `seq` | integer | Optional. See below. |
| `ttl` | integer | Optional, `>= 0`. Omit on create and the job gets 600. Negative: `ttl must be >= 0`. |

Unknown fields are ignored. JSON `null` on `title`, `link`, `note`, `progress`, `seq`, or `ttl` means omitted. On the daemon, JSON `null` for `agent`, `job_id`, or `state` is `invalid json`. On the relay, `null` for `agent` or `job_id` is treated as blank and then fails with `agent is required` or `job_id is required`. `null` for `state` is `invalid json` on both. There are no other job fields.

Schema: <https://statuspan.com/schema/job-update.schema.json>.

## Merge and seq

Current state is one card per `(agent, job_id)`. Every post is appended first. Then it merges, or it does not.

- A missing `seq` is newer. The post always applies, even if the card already has a seq. The stored seq is left as it was.
- A present `seq` applies when the card has no seq yet, or when the new seq is strictly greater.
- An equal or lower seq is stored in history with `applied: false` and does not change title, state, progress, link, note, ttl, seq, or `updated_at`.
- `applied` on the HTTP response is true if any item in the batch changed a card. An ignored seq is still HTTP 200.
- `finished_at` is set the first time a card becomes `done` or `failed`. Moving back to `queued`, `running`, or `blocked` clears it.
- History on the card keeps the last 20 events, oldest first. The daemon's global feed keeps the last 200, newest first.
- A heartbeat that repeats the same seq does not move `updated_at`, so a running job can still stall. Omit `seq`, or send a greater one, to refresh the clock.
- `n` on a daemon event, and `cursor` on a relay event, are the log id. They are not `seq`. Do not send `n` or `cursor` as if they were `seq`.

`statuspan ls` prints the job id when the title is empty. Its STALLED column is `ABANDONED`, `STALLED`, or `-`.

## Local CLI

`statuspan` with no arguments, or with a leading dash, is `serve`. `version`, `-version`, and `--version` must be the first argument. Untagged builds print `statuspan 0.2.0`. Release builds replace that with ldflags.

Exit code is 1 on error. The message is prefixed `statuspan: `. `statuspan run` is the exception: it exits with the wrapped command's status. A command that cannot be started is 127. Missing `--agent`, `--job`, or the command is 2. Unknown flags and invalid `--ttl` or `--heartbeat` on `run` are also 2, and the command does not start. A reporting misconfiguration does not change `run`'s exit code.

### statuspan serve

```text
statuspan [serve] [--addr host:port] [--data dir]
          [--abandon-after DUR] [--abandon-waiting-after DUR]
          [--relay-url URL] [--relay-workspace NAME] [--relay-token-file PATH]
```

| Flag | Default | Env | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--addr` | `127.0.0.1:4477` | `STATUSPAN_ADDR` | Listen address. Loopback only: `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, or `localhost`. Anything else is refused. |
| `--data` | OS config dir + `statuspan` | `STATUSPAN_DATA` | Data directory. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/statuspan`. Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/statuspan` or `~/.config/statuspan`. If neither home nor config dir resolves: `./statuspan-data`. |
| `--abandon-after` | `24h` | `STATUSPAN_ABANDON_AFTER` | Go duration (`24h`, `168h`, `0`). Silence before a stalled running job is abandoned. `0` disables that category. An explicit flag wins over the env. |
| `--abandon-waiting-after` | `168h` | `STATUSPAN_ABANDON_WAITING_AFTER` | Silence before a queued or blocked job is abandoned. `0` disables it. Not multiplied by `ttl`. |
| `--relay-url` | empty | `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL` | Relay base URL. Wins over the env and over `relay.json`. |
| `--relay-workspace` | empty | `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE` | Workspace name. Same precedence. |
| `--relay-token-file` | empty | `STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN` | File containing the read token (`spr_...`), one line, trimmed. The env is the token itself, not a path. |

Relay config order is flag, then environment, then `relay.json` in the data directory. If URL, workspace, or read token is set and another of the three is missing, serve exits instead of going local. If none are set, the daemon never calls out.

`relay.json`:

```json
{"url":"https://relay.example.com","workspace":"home","read_token":"<read token>"}
```

`chmod 600` that file. The read token is not logged and is not returned by `/healthz`.

The HTTP server's read-header timeout is 10 seconds. SIGINT or SIGTERM shuts it down within 3 seconds.

### statuspan post

```text
statuspan post --agent A --job ID [--state STATE] [--title T] [--progress N]
               [--link URL] [--note N] [--seq N] [--ttl S]
               [--url ENDPOINT | --addr host:port | --relay URL --workspace NAME (--token TOKEN | --token-file PATH)]
```

| Flag | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | empty | Required. |
| `--job` | empty | Required. This is `job_id`. |
| `--state` | empty | Sent as `""` when omitted, which leaves an existing job's state. A new job still needs a real state. |
| `--title` | omitted | Sent only if you pass the flag. `--title ""` clears it. |
| `--link` | omitted | Same as title. |
| `--note` | omitted | Same as title. |
| `--progress` | omitted | Integer 0 through 100. The CLI checks the range. |
| `--ttl` | omitted | Integer `>= 0`. The CLI checks it. |
| `--seq` | epoch ms | Integer. When the flag is omitted the CLI sends epoch milliseconds, strictly increasing in the process. An older or equal value is ignored by the server. |
| `--url` | empty | Full jobs endpoint, for example `http://127.0.0.1:14477/api/jobs`. Env `STATUSPAN_URL` when the flag is omitted and `--addr` was not passed. Not combined with a relay post. |
| `--addr` | `127.0.0.1:4477` | Env `STATUSPAN_ADDR`. Used only for a local post when `--url` and `STATUSPAN_URL` are unset. |
| `--relay` | empty | Env `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL` when the flag is omitted. |
| `--workspace` | empty | Env `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE` when the flag is omitted. |
| `--token` | empty | Write token. Env `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` when neither token flag is passed. |
| `--token-file` | empty | File with the write token. Cannot be combined with `--token`. Env `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` when neither token flag is passed and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` is empty. |

Local post timeout is 10 seconds. The command prints the JSON body. Status 300 or higher is an error.

If any of relay URL, workspace, or write token is set, all three are required. For `post`, a partial set, an unreadable token file, a bad `--url` or `--addr`, or `--url` combined with a relay fails and does not post to the local daemon. For `run`, that same misconfiguration prints one warning on stderr and the wrapped command still runs, with no posts. Leave all of them unset to post locally. The daemon's read token (`STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN`) is not the post token. `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` supplies the write token from a file when `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` is unset. The token is not printed.

Relay post: `POST {relay}/v1/w/{workspace}/jobs` with `Authorization: Bearer {write token}` and the same JSON. Timeout 10 seconds. A relay error prints the HTTP status and the relay's `error` string.

### statuspan run

```text
statuspan run --agent NAME --job ID [--title T] [--ttl SEC] [--heartbeat SEC] [--link URL] [--recurring]
              [--url ENDPOINT | --addr host:port | --relay URL --workspace NAME (--token TOKEN | --token-file PATH)]
              [--verbose] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]
```

`--agent` defaults to `STATUSPAN_AGENT`. The title defaults to the job id. `--ttl` defaults to 600. Heartbeats default to `min(ttl/2, 60s)` with a 10 second floor. `--heartbeat SEC` replaces that interval and has no floor.

Normal mode posts `running` at progress 0, then periodic `running` heartbeats, then `done` at progress 100 (`Completed in <duration>`) on exit 0 or `failed` (`Exited with code N after <duration>`) otherwise. Seq is epoch milliseconds, strictly increasing in the process. Posts before the command exits are fire-and-forget with about a 2 second timeout. The final post is awaited, also about 2 seconds. If StatusPan is down, the command still runs. StatusPan exits with the command's status. A signal is `128` plus the signal number. The child stays in StatusPan's process group, so an interactive command stays in the terminal foreground. StatusPan catches SIGINT and SIGTERM so it can post the final status. It forwards SIGTERM to the child. It forwards SIGINT only when stdin is not a terminal, because a terminal already delivered SIGINT to the foreground process group. `--verbose` prints board warnings on stderr. A reporting misconfiguration (partial relay settings, unreadable token file, bad `--url` or `--addr`, or `--url` combined with a relay) always prints one warning on stderr, posts nothing, and still exits with the command's status. The token is not printed.

`--recurring` makes no HTTP request while the command runs and none on exit 0. A non-zero exit posts one `failed`. That is the recurring-job rule: a healthy routine stays off the board, and a failure shows under Needs attention. Post `done` yourself once it is resolved. Use `blocked` only when you actually asked a human.

If the command cannot be started, both modes post `failed` with a note like `Could not start: ...` and StatusPan exits 127. Missing `--agent`, `--job`, or the command exits 2 and runs nothing.

Relay flags and `STATUSPAN_URL` / `--url` / `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` match `post`, with one difference: `post` returns the configuration error, and `run` warns and still runs the command.

### statuspan agent

`statuspan skill` is an alias.

| Command | What it prints or does |
| --- | --- |
| `statuspan agent`, `statuspan agent print`, `statuspan agent skill` | The full skill, including YAML frontmatter, on stdout. |
| `statuspan agent prompt` | A short snippet with no frontmatter, for AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. |
| `statuspan agent json` | Indented discovery JSON (name, version, docs, commands, env, endpoints, states, payload fields, reporting rules) and a trailing newline. Version is the binary version. |
| `statuspan agent install` | Writes `SKILL.md` for local agents. |
| `statuspan agent --help` | Lists the commands and install flags. |

Install flags:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--target` | `auto` | `auto`, `agents`, `claude`, `cursor`, `codex`, `all`, or a comma-separated list. Unknown names error. |
| `--dir PATH` | empty | Write `PATH/SKILL.md` instead of the tool targets. |
| `--home PATH` | the user's home | Overrides `$HOME` for the tool directories. |
| `--dry-run` | false | Print `would install <path>` for each target and write nothing. |

`auto` always writes `~/.agents/skills/statuspan/SKILL.md`. It also writes `~/.claude`, `~/.cursor`, and `~/.codex` copies when that directory already exists. An explicit target is created even when the directory is new. `all` writes all four. Files are written atomically (temp file, then rename), mode `0644`. New directories are mode `0755`. Each installed path is printed on its own line. The skill tells agents to keep healthy recurring jobs off the board, to push `blocked` or `failed` when a routine needs a person or has failed, and to push `done` once it is resolved. It also says a StatusPan failure must not block the real work.

### statuspan ls

`statuspan ls [--addr host:port]`. `GET /api/jobs`. Prints `no jobs`, or a table: AGENT, JOB, STATE, PROG, ELAPSED, STALLED, TITLE, NOTE. Timeout 10 seconds.

### statuspan clear

`statuspan clear --yes [--section attention|progress|queued|done] [--addr host:port]`. Without `--yes` it changes nothing and exits 1. With no `--section`, it deletes every job and its history (`DELETE /api/jobs?confirm=all`) and prints `deleted N` and the backup path. `--section done` (or `attention`, `progress`, `queued`) deletes only that section, prints `deleted N`, and does not print a backup. An unknown `--section` is an error and does not call the daemon.

### statuspan version / help

`statuspan version`, `statuspan -version`, `statuspan --version`.

`statuspan help`, `-h`, `--help`, or `-help` prints usage to stdout and exits 0. The usage line for agents is: `AI agents: run 'statuspan agent' for instructions or 'statuspan agent install' to install the skill.` Any other first word is `unknown command "..." (try statuspan help)`.

## Local HTTP API

Base URL `http://127.0.0.1:4477`. No auth. No CORS headers. Loopback only, so a browser on another origin is not the client you want. JSON responses use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Errors are `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}` unless noted.

### GET /healthz

`200`:

```json
{"ok":true,"relay":{"configured":false,"last_ok":null,"cursor":0,"last_error":""}}
```

`configured` is false in local-only mode. `last_ok` is an RFC3339 timestamp after a successful relay poll, otherwise null. `cursor` is the last merged relay event id. `last_error` is empty when the last poll worked. The token is never included.

### GET /

The embedded board, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. This is the daemon UI, not the marketing site.

### GET /favicon.ico

`204` empty.

### POST /api/jobs

One JobUpdate or an array. `200`:

```json
{"ok":true,"applied":true}
```

`400` error strings include `unreadable body`, `body too large`, `empty body`, `invalid json`, `agent is required`, `job_id is required`, `agent must not contain / or \`, `job_id must not contain / or \`, `state must be queued, running, blocked, done, or failed`, `progress must be an integer from 0 to 100`, `ttl must be >= 0`. A store failure that is not a validation error is `500` with `error` set to that message.

### GET /api/jobs

`200`. Jobs are sorted by agent ascending, then `updated_at` descending, then `job_id` ascending. An empty board is `"jobs": []`.

```json
{
  "now": "2026-11-23T18:00:00Z",
  "jobs": [],
  "abandon_after_seconds": 86400,
  "abandon_waiting_after_seconds": 604800
}
```

Each job:

```json
{
  "agent": "MyBot",
  "job_id": "build-1",
  "title": "Build v1",
  "state": "running",
  "progress": 40,
  "link": "https://example.com",
  "seq": 1,
  "ttl": 600,
  "note": "almost there",
  "started_at": "2026-11-23T17:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-23T17:40:00Z",
  "elapsed_seconds": 2400,
  "stalled": false,
  "abandoned": false,
  "history": []
}
```

`link`, `note`, and `seq` are omitted when empty or unset, not sent as null. `finished_at` and `abandoned_at` are omitted until set. The example above includes `link`, `note`, and `seq` because they are set. `abandoned_at` is present only when `abandoned` is true. `elapsed_seconds` is the age from `started_at`, and for `done` or `failed` it stops at `finished_at`. It is never negative. `history` is the last 20 events, oldest first. `deleted` appears only on a live delete event (see SSE), not on a listed job.

### GET /api/jobs/{agent}/{job_id}

`200` with that job object. `404` `{"ok":false,"error":"not found"}`.

### DELETE /api/jobs/{agent}/{job_id}

Removes one job and appends a delete tombstone. `200` `{"ok":true,"deleted":true}`. `deleted` is false when the job was already gone. That is still 200. Invalid ids are `400`.

### DELETE /api/jobs

Deletes every job, or one board section. Requires confirmation. The query wins over a JSON body.

- `confirm=all` deletes every job and its history. The daemon copies the log to `jobs-backup-<unix>.jsonl` first, then truncates the log.
- `confirm=attention`, `progress`, `queued`, or `done` deletes only the jobs in that section. Each one gets a delete tombstone. The rest of the log, and the other jobs, stay. There is no backup.
- Sections match the board. Attention is failed, blocked, stalled, and abandoned, including an abandoned queued or blocked job. Progress is a healthy running job. Queued is queued and not abandoned. Done is done.
- Query `?confirm=...`, or a JSON body `{"confirm":"..."}`. If the query contains `confirm`, the body is ignored.
- A missing confirm, or any other value, is `400` `confirm must be "all", "attention", "progress", "queued", or "done"`. The board does not change.
- Invalid JSON is `400` `invalid json`.

`200` for `confirm=all`:

```json
{"ok":true,"deleted":2,"backup":"/path/to/jobs-backup-1764000000.jsonl"}
```

`backup` is the absolute path of the copy. `deleted` is how many jobs were removed. A second clear of an empty board returns `deleted: 0` and another backup file. A failure to copy or truncate is `500`.

`200` for a section:

```json
{"ok":true,"deleted":2,"section":"done"}
```

`section` is the confirm value. `deleted` is 0 when that section was already empty, and the live stream gets no snapshot in that case. A section clear with `deleted` greater than 0 publishes one snapshot of the remaining board. A later post for a cleared `job_id` can bring that job back.

### GET /api/events

Query:

- `limit`. Default 200. `0` returns `"events": []`. A negative or non-integer value is `400` `invalid limit`. The global feed is capped at 200 even if you ask for more.
- `agent`. When set, events are that agent's, newest first, and they are not capped at 200 unless you also set `limit`.

`200`:

```json
{"now":"2026-11-23T18:00:00Z","events":[]}
```

An event, newest first:

```json
{
  "n": 4,
  "agent": "MyBot",
  "job_id": "build-1",
  "state": "running",
  "progress": 40,
  "note": "almost there",
  "title": "Build v1",
  "link": "https://example.com",
  "ts": "2026-11-23T17:40:00Z",
  "applied": true,
  "seq": 2,
  "kind": "update"
}
```

Empty optional strings are omitted. `kind` is `update` or `delete`. `applied` is false when seq lost.

### GET /api/stream

Server-Sent Events. `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`. A comment line `: keepalive` is sent every 15 seconds.

On connect, one snapshot, which is the same board as `GET /api/jobs` plus the recent event feed:

```text
event: snapshot
data: {"now":"...","jobs":[],"events":[],"abandon_after_seconds":86400,"abandon_waiting_after_seconds":604800}
```

Then one event per applied change:

```text
event: job
data: {"agent":"MyBot","job_id":"build-1","state":"running","stalled":false,"abandoned":false,"history":[]}
```

A delete is a `job` event with `"deleted": true` and a one-item history of `kind: "delete"`. An ignored seq does not emit a job event. If the response cannot flush, the status is `500` and the body is plain text `streaming unsupported`.

## Self-hosted relay

`relay/` is a Cloudflare Worker with one SQLite Durable Object per workspace. You deploy it yourself. The marketing site does not host your jobs. The same steps are on https://statuspan.com/relay. If you do not want to run Cloudflare yourself, Hosted Relay is the no-setup option: https://statuspan.com/cloud.

Cloud and remote agents (for example Cursor cloud agents, CI, and other servers) cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on your machine. They must post to a relay with a write token stored as a secret. The local daemon pulls those jobs in.

A free Cloudflare account and Node.js are enough.

### 1. Deploy

```bash
cd relay
npm install
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy
```

`wrangler deploy` prints the `workers.dev` URL.

### 2. Admin secret

Never commit it.

```bash
openssl rand -hex 32 > admin-token
npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_TOKEN < admin-token
chmod 600 admin-token
```

`ADMIN_TOKEN` is the Worker secret. Bots do not send it. It creates workspaces and mints, lists, and revokes tokens.

### 3. Workspace and tokens

`RELAY_URL` is the `workers.dev` URL from deploy.

```bash
export RELAY_URL=https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(cat admin-token)
node scripts/admin.mjs create-workspace home
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind write --agent MyBot --label laptop --out write-token
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind read --label board --out read-token
chmod 600 write-token read-token
```

`--out` writes only the token (mode 0600) and prints `saved to <path>`. `list` prints token ids, kinds, agents, and labels, not the secrets. `revoke` takes the token id.

- A write token belongs to one agent. It is post-only and cannot read the board.
- A read token feeds the board (list, poll, and stream) and cannot post.
- The admin token creates workspaces and mints, lists, and revokes tokens. Never give it to bots.

### 4. Point the daemon at the relay

`relay.json` goes in the data directory. On macOS that is `~/Library/Application Support/statuspan/relay.json`.

```json
{"url":"https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev","workspace":"home","read_token":"<paste the read token>"}
```

`chmod 600` that file and restart the daemon. On start, and about every 3 seconds after that, it polls the workspace and merges events into the local board. Alternative environment variables, which win over the file: `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN`. Flags win over both. If the URL, workspace, or read token is set and another of the three is missing, serve exits instead of going local.

### 5. Agents post

Set `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` (or `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` as a secret). Then `statuspan post` or `statuspan run`, or curl with `Authorization: Bearer`. Store the write token as a secret. A remote agent cannot fall back to `127.0.0.1`.

### Connect another machine to your relay

Use this when a second computer, a cloud agent, or CI should post to the same board. Those agents cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on the machine that runs the board.

Token roles:

| Token | Role |
| --- | --- |
| write | Per machine or agent. Post only. Cannot read the board. |
| read | Local daemon and board only. Cannot post. |
| admin | Mint and revoke tokens, create workspaces. Never give it to bots. |

1. On the machine that has the admin token, from `relay/`:

```bash
export RELAY_URL="https://<your-relay>.workers.dev"
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(cat admin-token)
node scripts/admin.mjs mint <workspace> --kind write --agent <agent-name> --label <machine-label> --out write-token
```

The command is `node scripts/admin.mjs mint <workspace> --kind read|write [--agent <name>] [--label <label>] [--out <path>]`. A write token requires `--agent`. `--label` is optional and should name the machine. `--out` writes only the token (mode 0600) and prints `saved to <path>`. The token is scoped to that agent name; posts from the new machine must use the same `--agent`. `RELAY_URL` and `ADMIN_TOKEN` come from the environment, or `--relay-url` / `--admin-token-file`.

2. On the new machine, save the token to `~/.config/statuspan/token` (`chmod 600`). Never put the token in shell history or chat. Prefer copying the file minted with `--out`, or pasting it into an editor. Do not `echo` the token on the command line.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/statuspan
# copy write-token onto the new machine as ~/.config/statuspan/token
chmod 600 ~/.config/statuspan/token
```

3. On the new machine, set these and persist them in your shell rc (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`):

```bash
export STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL="https://<your-relay>.workers.dev"
export STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE="<workspace>"
export STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE="$HOME/.config/statuspan/token"
```

4. Verify. Post a test job (the agent name must match the token) and check the local board within a few seconds:

```bash
statuspan post --agent "<agent-name>" --job connect-test --state running --note "from the new machine"
```

Then look for that job on the board, or `curl -s "http://${STATUSPAN_ADDR:-127.0.0.1:4477}/api/jobs"`.

The rest of this section is the relay HTTP API.

Workspace names match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`.

Tokens are random 32 bytes. A write token is prefixed `spw_`. A read token is prefixed `spr_`. Only the SHA-256 of the token is stored.

- A write token is scoped to one agent. It can `POST` updates for that agent. It cannot list jobs, poll events, or open the stream (`403` `write token cannot read`). Posting any other agent name in the batch is `403` `token is scoped to a different agent`.
- A read token can `GET` jobs, events, and the stream. It cannot post (`403` `read token cannot write`). It has no agent.
- Missing or unknown bearer is `401` `{"ok":false,"error":"unauthorized"}`.
- A workspace that was never created is `404` `workspace not found`, including for a token check.
- A bad workspace name is `400` `invalid workspace`.
- Wrong method is `405` `method not allowed`, with an `Allow` header.
- Unknown paths are `404` `not found`.
- An unexpected failure is `500` `internal error`. The Worker does not return the internal message.
- No CORS headers.

`GET /healthz` on the relay is not the daemon's JSON. It is `200` text `ok\n` (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`).

### POST /v1/w/{workspace}/jobs

Bearer write token. Same body and the same field rules as `POST /api/jobs`. Same `200` `{"ok":true,"applied":true|false}`.

Extra `400` strings: `invalid content-length`, `too many updates`.

### GET /v1/w/{workspace}/jobs

Bearer read token. `200`:

```json
{"now":"2026-11-23T18:00:00.000Z","jobs":[]}
```

Jobs have the same shape as the daemon, including `stalled` and `abandoned`, computed with the fixed 24h and 7 day windows. There is no `abandon_after_seconds` field. There is no single-job GET and no DELETE.

### GET /v1/w/{workspace}/events

Bearer read token.

| Query | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `since` | Exclusive cursor. Default 0. Non-digits: `400` `invalid since`. |
| `limit` | Default 200. `0` returns no events. Above 1000 is capped at 1000. Non-digits: `400` `invalid limit`. |

`200`, events in ascending cursor order (this is the poll direction, oldest of the page first):

```json
{
  "now": "2026-11-23T18:00:00.000Z",
  "events": [],
  "next_cursor": 0
}
```

`next_cursor` is the cursor of the last event in this page, or `since` when the page is empty. Relay events include `cursor` and `n` set to the same id, plus the same fields as a daemon event. `kind` is `update`. The relay keeps at most 50000 events. Job history on a job object is the last 20, oldest first.

### GET /v1/w/{workspace}/stream

Bearer read token. SSE, `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`. Keepalive comment every 15 seconds.

```text
event: snapshot
data: {"now":"...","jobs":[],"events":[]}

event: job
data: {"agent":"MyBot","job_id":"build-1","state":"running","stalled":false,"abandoned":false,"history":[]}
```

The snapshot's `events` are the 200 newest. It does not include the abandon-window fields. Later frames are applied job views only.

### Admin routes

Bearer `ADMIN_TOKEN`, not an `spr_` or `spw_` token.

| Method and path | Body | Success |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/admin/workspaces/{workspace}` | none | `200` `{"ok":true,"created":true}`. `created` is false if it already existed. |
| `POST /v1/admin/workspaces/{workspace}/tokens` | `{"kind":"write","agent":"MyBot","label":"laptop"}` or `{"kind":"read","label":"board"}` | `200` includes `id`, `token` (shown once), `kind`, `agent`, `label`, `created`. |
| `GET /v1/admin/workspaces/{workspace}/tokens` | none | `200` `{"ok":true,"tokens":[{"id","kind","agent","label","created"}]}`. No secrets. |
| `DELETE /v1/admin/workspaces/{workspace}/tokens/{id}` | none | `200` `{"ok":true,"revoked":true}`. Unknown id: `404` `not found`. |

Mint rules: `kind` is `read` or `write`. A write token requires `agent`. A read token must not set `agent` (`read tokens cannot set agent`). `label` is an optional string up to 200 characters. Empty body is `400` `empty body`.

### How the daemon pulls

On start, and about every 3 seconds after a success, the daemon calls:

```text
GET {url}/v1/w/{workspace}/events?since={cursor}&limit=1000
Authorization: Bearer {read token}
```

It merges each `update` with `ApplyAt` so the event's own timestamp is kept, using the same seq rules as a local post. The cursor is saved in `relay-cursor` in the data directory. A repeated cursor is a no-op. Failures back off, with jitter, from 1 second, doubling, up to about 60 seconds. Errors are logged without the token. Merged jobs go out on the local SSE stream.

Point `statuspan serve` at the relay with the flags above, or with `relay.json` in the data directory (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/statuspan/relay.json`). `chmod 600` that file. Restart after changing it. Alternative environment: `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN`.

Post from an agent that is not on this machine. It cannot use `127.0.0.1`. Store the write token as a secret (`STATUSPAN_TOKEN` or `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE`) together with `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL` and `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`:

```bash
curl --max-time 2 -s -X POST "$RELAY_URL/v1/w/home/jobs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUSPAN_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent":"MyBot","job_id":"build-1","title":"Build v1","state":"running","seq":1}' \
  || true
```

Or:

```bash
statuspan post --relay "$RELAY_URL" --workspace home --token-file write-token \
  --agent MyBot --job build-1 --state running --progress 55 --note halfway
```

Read:

```bash
curl -s "$RELAY_URL/v1/w/home/jobs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat read-token)"
curl -s "$RELAY_URL/v1/w/home/events?since=0" -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat read-token)"
```

## Fire and forget

If the post fails or times out, continue the real work. Do not retry in a loop. Do not wait on the board.

Bash:

```bash
curl --max-time 2 -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4477/api/jobs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent":"MyBot","job_id":"build-1","title":"Build v1","state":"running","progress":40,"seq":1}' \
  || true
```

Python, standard library only:

```python
import json
import urllib.request

def statuspan_post(update):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://127.0.0.1:4477/api/jobs",
        data=json.dumps(update).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=2) as resp:
            resp.read()
    except Exception:
        pass

statuspan_post({
    "agent": "Writer",
    "job_id": "docs-refresh",
    "title": "Refresh the docs",
    "state": "running",
    "seq": 1,
})
```

Node.js:

```javascript
async function statuspanPost(update) {
  try {
    await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4477/api/jobs", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(update),
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000),
    });
  } catch {
    // StatusPan is optional. Keep working.
  }
}

await statuspanPost({
  agent: "Builder",
  job_id: "build-1",
  title: "Build v1",
  state: "running",
  progress: 40,
  seq: 1,
});
```

For the relay, change the URL to `https://relay.example.com/v1/w/home/jobs` and add `Authorization: Bearer <spw_ write token>`. Same body. Same timeout. Same ignore-on-failure rule.

## Agent guidance

Pick one `job_id` slug per piece of work and keep it: `build-1`, `docs-refresh`. Reuse it for every heartbeat. A new slug is a new card. Do not put secrets in any field. Do not use `/` or `\` in `agent` or `job_id`.

Emit:

- `queued` when the work is accepted and you have not started.
- `running` as you start, and again as a heartbeat before `ttl` seconds (default 600). Send progress or a note. Increase `seq`, or omit `seq`.
- `blocked` when you need a person. Say why in `note`.
- `done` when you reach the finish line. That is what clears a card out of Needs attention.
- `failed` when you stop unsuccessfully. Include a useful `note`.

Never block real work if StatusPan is offline. The snippets above are the pattern.

Recurring jobs, in full:

- Healthy recurring jobs and scheduled routines stay off the board. A daily or hourly run that is going fine must not get a card.
- If a recurring job becomes `blocked` or `failed`, it must be pushed so it surfaces in Needs attention.
- Once that recurring job is fixed or unblocked, push `done` so it clears out of Needs attention.
- A routine that produces a separate, finishable piece of work can post that work under its own `job_id`. A quiet run posts nothing.

Do not post `stalled` or `abandoned`. Do not clear the board, or a section of it, unless a person asked (`statuspan clear --yes`, or `statuspan clear --yes --section done`).
